* * * **
 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
On 04.07.2023 at about 07.20 p.m, the petitioner was pedestrian on extreme correct side of Bengaluru - (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 Kanakapura Road and when he reached in front of Anjaneya Temple Road, Thoppaganahalli Village, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Main Road, Kanakapura Town and Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time

the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-42-Y-1408 has driven from Bengaluru side towards Kanakapura side, with very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from behind and caused the accident, in which petitioner was going on extreme left side road by walk.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to CDSIMER,
Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar hospital, Harohalli, wherein he took first aid treatment, immediately further management shifted to Re-life hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 04.07.2023 to 12.07.2023 and after conservative treatment, the petitioner still continuing the follow-up treatment and bedrest and he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment and attendant charges etc.,.
Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 70 years and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m by doing Agricultural works and having 02 acres irrigation land.

Due to accidental injuries, he has undergone severe (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 pain, bedridden and cannot do his routine work and he was not get earlier physical fitness and cannot chewing food, partial headache, double vision and cannot speak properly, loss of partial memory, loss of hearing and cannot urinate and suffering permanent disability and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings and hardship, he cannot attend his work permanently, resulted in loss of earning and put to great financial hardship and untold misery and depressed and further submits that there is 02 days delay in lodging complaint as he was under treatment with critical condition,
therefore he lodged belated complaint.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of above said offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Kanakapura Traffic Police have registered a case against rider of said offending Motor Cycle.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay Kariyappa vs Mariyappa on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152666966/
2 compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with cost and interest.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal, but only the respondent No.1 has filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the accident in question took place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner herself who was darting across the road without observing the flow of traffic on the busy road and admits that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in respect of the offending Motor Cycle which was valid as on the date of accident.

However, the liability of this respondent to indemnify the insured in respect of said policy is as per the statute, terms, limitations and conditions of the policy and compliance of 64VB of Insurance Act and the owner of the vehicle willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the Motor Cycle and did not valid permit to ply on the road as on the date of accident and as such there is a breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.

The compensation claimed is excessive, (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 04.07.2023 at about 07.20 p.m, in front of Anjaneya Temple Road, Thoppaganahalli Village, Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Kanakapura, Ramanagara District, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-42-Y-1408 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence, hence, respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.

(SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 Kariyappa vs Mariyappa on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152666966/
3

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1
In affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle by its rider, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Kanakapura Traffic Police against rider of offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.2 is the complaint shows that due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motor Cycle the accident took place and petitioner sustained injuries and he has stated explanation for delay of 02 days in lodging complaint (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 that as he was accompanied with his father who was taking treatment in the hospital, therefore he lodged belated complaint.

Ex.P.3 to 5 are the Spot Mahazar, Seizer Mahazar and Sketch showing place of accident on Bengaluru - Kanakapura Road, Thoppaganahalli Village, in front of Anjaneya Temple Road,
Kasaba Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV report which discloses that involvement of offending Motor Cycle in the accident.

Ex.P.7 is Wound certificate which shows the petitioner sustained head injury of occipital region, multiple abrasions at eyes and lower limb, abrasion at right pelvic region and bleeding from left ear and said injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.8 is the important document Investigation Officer.
After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.9 and 10 are the Discharge summaries which shows that the petitioner sustained head injury occipital region, multiple abrasion at upper and lower limb,
abrasion at right pelvic region and bleeding from left ear and Urinary tract infection-S/P SPC insertion on 04.07.2023, ?SAI- treated conservatively, massive ascites and urethral stricture.
Ex.P.14 is Aadhaar card of petitioner.
To (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 disprove the case of petitioner, the respondents have not lead evidence.

The petitioner got examined MRO at Medax hospital and he has produced Authorization letter and entire Case sheet as per Ex.P.15 and 16 and in his cross-examination he admits that in their hospital MLC has not been registered and also Police intimation has not given and as per Ex.P.16 there is no mention of RTA.

Further, another Medical Record In-charge at Re-life hospital is examined as PW.3 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC extract, Police intimation and Inpatient case sheet as per Kariyappa vs Mariyappa on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152666966/
4 Ex.P.17 and 20.

On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending Motor Cycle.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 PW.1 in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 70 years and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m by doing Agricultural works and having 02 acres irrigation land and he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment and attendant charges etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost his income, earning capacity and become permanent disabled.

12. But in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he has sustained any percentage of permanent,
physical or functional disability due to accidental injuries.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding avocation and income and disability certificate and in the absence of evidence of the doctor, the petitioner has not sustained any loss of income either during laid up period or future loss of income.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income and also loss of income during laid up period.

13. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Discharge summaries as per Ex.P.9 and 10 (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 which shows he was inpatient in Re-life hospital, Bengaluru and Medax hospital, Bengaluru, totally for 20 days.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment,
towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
14. Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per Radiology reports, Case sheet and Inpatient case sheet and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.12 and Prescriptions as per Ex.P.13, which amounts to Rs.2,19,388/-.
To disprove the said medical expenses, the respondents have not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,19,388/- under this head.

16. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the Kariyappa vs Mariyappa on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152666966/
5 discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

17. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 2.
Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 3. Medical Expenses 2,19,388-00 4. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00
unhappiness  Total 3,09,388-00 18.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,09,388/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

19. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal,
but not filed objections and not contested the matter.

The respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4590/2023 and filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its defence.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,09,388/- (Rupees Three lakhs nine thousand three hundred and eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,09,388/- (Rupees Three lakhs nine thousand three hundred and eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
